title: Gratitude for joy
hook: Marcus Aurelius opens his private notebook with a whole book of thank-yous, person by person

segments.voice: Yesterday's line: as it flies. Mary was sent running with her joy, and Blake said don't bind it. Today, the joy goes back to the person who gave it.

segments.voice: Thank-you notes have a reputation as a chore your relatives make you do after birthdays. A Roman emperor wrote them anyway, to himself. Marcus Aurelius kept a notebook, the book we call the Meditations. And before he writes a single rule for his own life, he writes a list of people and what each one gave him. The very first line, in George Long's translation: "From my grandfather Verus I learned good morals and the government of my temper."
screen: `THANK-YOU NOTES: A CHORE?` → `AN EMPEROR'S NOTEBOOK.` → `FROM MY GRANDFATHER VERUS…`

segments.voice: Then his mother: reverence, generosity, and a simple way of living, far from the habits of the rich. A teacher named Rusticus: for lending him the discourses of Epictetus from his own collection. On it goes, person by person, a whole first book of debts. It ends by thanking the gods for good grandparents, good parents, good teachers, good friends. That's the Stoic practice at the front door of the Meditations: before you work on yourself, name what you were given, and by whom. Marcus didn't think he made himself. Here's one to tell a friend tonight: an emperor's private book starts with pages of thank-yous. And notice what he thanks people for. Not riches or rank, mostly. Good things: a temper learned, a book shared, a way of living watched up close. That's gratitude for joy: going back to the person behind a happy thing and naming exactly what it gave you. Not "thanks for everything." The specific thing. From you, I learned this. From you, I got that. It closes the circle on a week of joy: savored, shared, feasted, laughed at, let fly, and now thanked.
screen: `FROM MY GRANDFATHER VERUS.` · `RUSTICUS LENT HIM EPICTETUS.` · `NAME WHAT YOU WERE GIVEN.` · `THE SPECIFIC THING.` · then, large: `THANK YOU.`

segments.voice: Write one line by hand in the shape of Marcus's first book: from this person, I received this one good thing. A second line, if one comes. Then sit with their faces for the rest of the time, and send the line later if you like.
Gratitude for joy: thanking the person behind a happy thing, by name, for exactly what they gave, as Marcus did.
Your line: thank you. Said to a name, for the one specific thing they gave. Talk tomorrow.
